thread:
Ananya Rao: customer hit 400 JSON parse error when sending an orders batch with json-mode. They say it used to ignore extra keys. Request id: req_01F9Z2. Also reporting higher token billing and latency spikes.
Kevin Park: can you paste the exact request payload and the raw error body? Which json_mode are they using?
Ananya Rao: here's a sanitized repro — they're sending via a streaming client, and our parser errors because an item gets split across chunks. Repro curl + truncated payload below (sanitized).
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\n   \"json_mode\":\"strict\",\n   \"orders\":[\n     {\"order_id\":\"o-100\",\"items\":[{\"id\":\"sku_1\",\"qty\":1}]},\n     {\"order_id\":\"o-101\",\"items\":[{\"id\":\"sku_2\",\"qty\":2,\"coupon\":\"WINTER\"}]},\n     {\"order_id\":\"o-102\",\"items\":[{\"id\":'\n```
Ananya Rao: server returned 400 with body: `{"error":"JSON parse error: unexpected token at offset 356 (extra key 'coupon' in array item)"}` — but the customer expects extra keys like `coupon` to be tolerated.
support-bot: created support ticket SUP-4321 and attached request id req_01F9Z2.
Maria Chen: this looks like two separate problems: 1) client-side streaming/chunking can split JSON tokens mid-object; 2) the strict schema validation is rejecting keys we previously tolerated. For streaming endpoints we need parser buffering across chunks to avoid splitting errors. For schema drift we can either (a) add an `allow_extra_keys` flag or (b) relax validation server-side for hosted customers.
Kevin Park: can you paste the raw bytes from the client-side log (pre-redaction) showing the chunk boundaries? Also confirm whether this customer is Hosted or Dedicated. If Hosted, we can apply a temporary tolerant flag on their tenant.
Ananya Rao: Hosted. attaching client log snippet (sanitized):
```
[client] SEND CHUNK 1 (256 bytes): ... \"id\":\"sku_2\",\"qty\":2,\"coupon\":\"WINTER\"}]},
[client] SEND CHUNK 2 (64 bytes): \"order_id\":\"o-102\",\"items\":\\[{\"id\":\"sku_3\",\"qty\":1\\}]\n[client] FIN
```
Ananya Rao: because chunk1 ended mid-object for the next order our streaming parser tried to validate the partial object and flagged `coupon` as an unexpected key — the `offset` in the error pointed into chunk1.
Maria Chen: immediate mitigations: ask customer to switch to non-streaming for the batch POST OR have them serialize the entire body before sending. Longer term: eng-runtime should update the streaming parser to buffer until a complete JSON token/object is available before applying schema validation. Also add an opt-in `tolerant_json` request flag so customers can opt out of strict rejection while we roll.
eng-runtime: we reproduced with the supplied chunks. Current streaming path validates per-object as soon as it sees closing braces from the chunk boundary; it doesn't always reconstruct tokens that cross boundaries. We'll implement a small buffer to ensure we only run schema validation on complete object boundaries. Also adding `ignore_unknown_fields` toggle for hosted customers. ETA: 48 hours for canary patch + 72 hours for rollout if no regressions.
Kevin Park: please also collect metrics — why did billing spike? Looks like a client retried twice after parse failure, doubling token usage. Create billing ticket and propose a one-off credit while we fix.
support-bot: created billing ticket BILL-987 linked to SUP-4321.
Ananya Rao: customer accepted temporary workaround (non-streaming) and asked for ETA. They also asked for a short doc snippet to explain safe streaming practices.
Maria Chen: I'll draft a brief KB: "Streaming best-practices: ensure chunk boundaries don't split JSON tokens; prefer whole-body POST for strict json_mode; set tolerant_json when using third-party clients that may chunk."
Kevin Park: escalating to eng-runtime with linked tickets SUP-4321 / BILL-987. Eng-runtime, please include regression test that simulates chunk-splitting with extra keys and ordering variations.
eng-runtime: will add tests and put a canary behind a feature flag. We'll post updates in this thread. :eyes: :gear:
Ananya Rao: thanks — will notify customer and confirm when they can switch back to streaming.
Kevin Park: marking as escalated, moving to priority-high until patch is live.
